extraction.Name: Elizabeth Dixon
extraction.Refused/Protested: did not want her patent to her 640 acre allotment when she got it, but she got a letter from the Superintendent of the Pine Ridge Agency, stating that her patent had been reported to the Tax Collector, and she would have taxes to pay in any event; so she accepted it
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: mortgaged 320 acres of her allotment, to Joe Skinner, of Gordon, Nebraska, for $1000.00, and since that time she has just kept the interest paid up on this loan
extraction.Buyer: Joe Skinner, of Gordon, Nebraska, for $1000.00
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: in 1923, the taxes being entirely behind, she mortgaged 320 acres of her allotment; some of the money she borrowed in 1923 went for taxes on her husband's estate; the taxes on this 320, situated in Bennett County, is away behind again
extraction.Occupation/Income: her only income is the lease money she receives from her allotment
extraction.NOTES: mentally competent; not in possession of very good health, being bothered with rheumatism especially; has one minor child to support, and that this child is bothered with heart trouble; husband has been dead since 1920; never received any help from the County or the Government; document No. 406; sworn November 19, 1928; 320 acres mortgaged situated in Bennett County
